hunt.justification: The MANTLEMAZE and Warlock ransomware chain uses sophisticated AI-evasion and kernel-impairment techniques that bypass traditional single-point detections. This phased hunt ensures that even if one stage is evasive, the correlation of the full attack lifecycle provides a definitive result.

scenario.summary: Mantlemaze and other threat actors are employing 'AI-Analysis Evasion' (A3) by embedding natural-language instructions in malware to trick automated scrutiny, often pairing it with kernel-level driver abuse to disable EDR. These techniques are observed alongside high-impact threats including vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler and ransomware attacks by groups like Warlock.

meta.rationale: Start by identifying any host running the reported hashes or processes matching the trojan names. Also include a wide behavioral scoop for processes running from user folders with non-system integrity, as these are common staging areas for trojanized utilities.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has gained access via trojanized software containing AI-analysis evasion code, then loaded vulnerable drivers to disable security tools before executing ransomware.

hunt.name: Trojanized Utilities and Kernel EDR Impairment
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the full lifecycle of an endpoint intrusion starting with trojanized utility execution, such as KMSAuto or PulseBrowser, which incorporates A3 (AI-Analysis Evasion) techniques. It follows the chain from initial access to kernel-level defense evasion using BYOVD (Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver) and concludes with mass file encryption indicative of Warlock ransomware. The phased approach ensures that later impact signals are analyzed in the context of the initial beachhead.

config.scoping_notes: Start by identifying any host running the reported hashes or processes matching the trojan names. Also include a wide behavioral scoop for processes running from user folders with non-system integrity, as these are common staging areas for trojanized utilities.
config.beyond_detection: A single rule on a trojan hash might be dismissed as a False Positive or PUAs. This hunt correlates the initial access with two critical follow-on behaviors: kernel driver tampering (BYOVD) and mass file encryption. The analyst weighs these across three different telemetry surfaces to confirm a high-confidence intrusion.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_original_file_name, process_hash_sha256, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{trojan_hashes}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_hash_sha256) || ',') > 0 OR LOWER(process_original_file_name) IN ('kmsauto net.exe', 'secoh-qad.exe', 'sample.exe', 'f_003914.exe') OR (LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\kmsauto net.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\secoh-qad.exe' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\sample.exe') OR ( (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\downloads\%') AND integrity_level != 'System' AND (process_original_file_name IS NULL OR process_original_file_name = '') ) ) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify initial beachheads by matching malicious processes by hash, original filename, or behavioral traits in user-writable paths.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts running reported malware or suspicious, unnamed binaries from user folders. Results define the scope for the rest of the hunt.

nodes.label: DNS queries to C2 or high-entropy domains

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) as lookups, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{c2_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0 OR (LENGTH(query_hostname) > 24 AND LOWER(query_hostname) NOT LIKE '%.local%' AND LOWER(query_hostname) NOT LIKE '%.internal%')) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
config.description: Detect network beacons to known malicious domains or anomalous high-entropy domains on scoped hosts.
config.expected_signal: DNS resolutions for reported C2 domains or long, complex hostnames which may represent DGA or C2 rotation. Silence suggests the beaconing infrastructure has rotated.

config.objective: Determine if the scoped hosts are confirmed beachheads. Specifically look for evidence of A3 evasion, such as binaries that have been flagged by AV but show execution, or unusual process trees originating from the trojanized utilities.
config.description: Evaluate whether the initial process, network, and file signals indicate a confirmed infection and look for A3 evasion indicators.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict of suspicious or malicious based on early intrusion evidence.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict citing specific rows from the process and DNS results.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, driver_path, driver_signature_subject, COUNT(*) as loads, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_kernel_extension_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) <= 3
config.description: Identify rare driver loads across the fleet that may represent the use of vulnerable drivers to disable security agents.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts loading rare drivers. Fleet-wide rarity is a strong indicator of manual BYOVD tampering to impair security tools.

primitive_config.label: Kernel EDR impairment via BYOVD
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, driver_path, driver_signature_subject, COUNT(*) as loads, MIN(time) as first_seen FROM hb_kernel_extension_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) <= 3
primitive_config.expected: A list of hosts loading rare drivers. Fleet-wide rarity is a strong indicator of manual BYOVD tampering to impair security tools.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, SUBSTR(file_name, INSTR(file_name, '.') + 1) as extension, COUNT(*) as file_count, MIN(time) as first_op FROM hb_file_activity WHERE activity_id IN (4, 5) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 HAVING file_count > 1000
config.description: Identify mass file modification activity indicative of ransomware encryption, grouping by file extension.
config.expected_signal: A process modifying over 1000 files, likely with a consistent extension. This distinguishes ransomware from typical application updates or temporary file cleanup.

primitive_config.label: High-volume file encryption (Impact)

primitive_config.expected: A process modifying over 1000 files, likely with a consistent extension. This distinguishes ransomware from typical application updates or temporary file cleanup.

config.objective: Evaluate the full attack chain. Confirm whether hosts with a confirmed beachhead (from Agent 1) have subsequently loaded rare drivers and performed mass file encryption.
config.description: Synthesize early beachhead evidence with follow-on EDR impairment and encryption signals to confirm a full ransomware intrusion.
config.expected_signal: A definitive malicious verdict for any host that shows the full progression from trojan to impact.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of malicious | suspicious, citing drivers and file counts.

config.question: the follow-on-triage-agent verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.condition: the follow-on-triage-agent verdict is malicious for at least one host
config.description: Direct immediate containment for malicious hosts and forensic review for suspicious activity.
Immediately contain the host to stop the encryption process and prevent lateral movement.
config.instructions: Isolate the host from the network and revoke any active credentials or administrative sessions that were active on the host at the time of the trojan execution.

config.description: Perform a deep dive into the A3 evasion techniques and the extent of driver tampering.
config.instructions: Review the binaries found on the scoped hosts for imperative language instructions meant to deceive AI analysts. Identify the vulnerable driver and verify whether its use corresponds to a known MANTLEMAZE variant.

config.description: Document the hunt outcome and convert effective behavioral signals into standing detections.
config.instructions: Record the hunt findings. If the ransomware-impact query correctly identified an intrusion, promote it to a standing detection rule. If A3 evasion was identified, ensure future analysis pipelines treat extracted sample text as evidence only.
